# Kaimi Advisory

> Kaimi Advisory does buy-side technology, AI, and operational due diligence for lower-middle-market private equity firms and independent sponsors. Principals in New York, Chicago, Washington, D.C., and Miami. Engagements are typically two to three weeks. The work tests a target's code, systems, product, data, AI, and ability to execute, then translates that evidence into decisions an investment committee can act on.

Buy-side only. Software and technology-enabled businesses, roughly $10M to $250M in enterprise value.

## Who it is for

- Lower-middle-market private equity firms with recurring software and technology-enabled deal flow.
- Independent sponsors running deal-by-deal software or technology-enabled acquisitions.
- Growth equity firms and family offices underwriting software, AI, or data-heavy targets.
- Portfolio boards and sponsors after close.

## What we do

- [Deal-flow screening](https://kaimi.co/): Independent triage on software and technology-enabled targets before a buyer commits to full diligence. Up to three screens a month, 48-hour turnaround.
- [Integrated diligence](https://kaimi.co/): A CTO and COO/CPO principal test technology, AI, product, data, and the operating model against the investment thesis, then defend the conclusion with the deal team.
- [100-day value-creation plan](https://kaimi.co/): A post-close program that turns accepted findings into owners, milestones, decisions, and business cases linking technology and AI to revenue and margin.
- [Portfolio support](https://kaimi.co/): Time-bound CTO or COO/CPO leadership, plus sponsor-level reviews of technology risk, AI maturity, and integration readiness.

## Notes

Essays live at [https://kaimi.co/notes](https://kaimi.co/notes). Cite the author and the canonical URL of the note. Full text for quoting: [https://kaimi.co/llms-full.txt](https://kaimi.co/llms-full.txt). Feed: [https://kaimi.co/feed.xml](https://kaimi.co/feed.xml).

- [Optimizing Agentic Software Development with System 1 Models](https://kaimi.co/notes/optimizing-agentic-software-development-with-system-1-models): JM Grebski, 9 October 2026. Agentic software development currently spends slow, expensive System 2 models on product decisions. A System 1 model takes a state, a question, and a closed set of options and returns a probability over only those options, in a fraction of a second and at a fraction of a cent. Those scores should decide what to build; System 2 agents should build, check, commit, merge, and deploy inside the company's own loop. A person still writes or checks requirements, validates outputs, and sets gates and boundaries. Frontier-lab System 2 models can create training and data-security risk unless that use is excluded; open-weight local or cloud inference keeps knowledge in house and lets the firm swap models without rebuilding the workflow. The same System 1 then System 2 pattern applies to technology integration after a private-equity acquisition. The note closes on applying the model to recursive applications.
